docs.title: What is CAS?
docs.text: The Continuous Architecture System (CAS) is a governed, decision-driven knowledge system designed to transform architecture from static documentation into a continuously updated and queryable operational asset.

docs.title: Core Rationale & Navigation
docs.text:
• Why CAS?: Rationale, traditional architecture governance challenges, and Shift-Left Governance.
  • how-cas-works: Operating loop (Prevent → Architecture Workflow → Detect & Correct).
  • operating-model: Core concepts (ADR, AEM, AID, AW).
  • Platform Documentation: Detailed technical platform documentation.

docs.title: How CAS Works
docs.text:
CAS operates as a dual-control governance loop:

  1. Prevent: CAS Agent Skills enforce architectural constraints directly during coding and refactoring.
  2. Architecture Workflow: Governed flows generate Architecture Work (AW), Architecture Evolution Maps (AEM), and Intent Documents (AID).
  3. Detect & Correct: Alignment Engine flags architectural drift and provides actionable remediation.

docs.title: CAS Architecture & Operating Model
docs.text:
CAS is built on decision-driven governance where the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) is the authoritative Single Source of Truth (SSOT).

  • ADR: Single Source of Truth for architecture decisions.
  • AEM: System state derived directly from decisions.
  • AID: Architectural intent and strategic direction.
  • AW: Authoritative architectural change backlog.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text: Traditional enterprise architecture relies heavily on static documentation to govern complex systems. While these artifacts capture initial strategic intent, they are inherently disconnected from the engineering reality. As systems evolve, a critical gap forms between the documented architecture and the actual implementation, leading to severe documentation drift and a loss of alignment. The fundamental problem is that static governance mechanisms cannot scale to meet the demands of modern delivery velocity without introducing unacceptable friction.

docs.title: Why Traditional Governance Breaks
docs.text: Architecture governance typically degrades not because of engineering failure, but due to systemic operational limitations. Manual review processes and point-in-time assessments are fundamentally incompatible with continuous delivery and agile execution. As an organisation scales, the administrative burden of maintaining architectural alignment across disconnected teams becomes unsustainable. This friction inevitably leads to architectural drift, where the system's operational reality diverges from strategic intent, creating hidden technical debt and operational risk.

docs.title: Shift-Left Governance
docs.text:
Traditional governance mechanisms operate too late in the delivery lifecycle, relying on post-implementation reviews, documentation reconciliation, and periodic oversight to detect architectural divergence. CAS shifts architecture governance directly into the software construction process itself, establishing preventive operational guardrails that guide implementation from the moment code is created while continuously detecting and correcting what still escapes those boundaries.

This creates a dual-governance operational model:

  • Preventive Governance — Governance aware onboarding, CAS Skills, coding agent operational guidance, specification-driven development workflows, and CI validation establish architectural boundaries before implementation diverges.
  • Corrective Governance — Continuous governance workflows, capability extraction, steering projection, evaluation, and operational reconciliation detect and correct architectural drift that still emerges during system evolution.

By embedding governance directly into software construction workflows, CAS transforms architecture from a passive review function into an active operational capability that continuously shapes repository evolution in real time. This governance aware software construction model becomes increasingly critical in environments where coding agents actively participate in delivery workflows.

docs.title: The Architectural Insight
docs.text: The resolution to this drift lies in shifting the paradigm from static documentation and reactive governance toward operational intelligence embedded directly into the software construction lifecycle. The core insight behind the Continuous Architecture System (CAS) is that architecture must operate as a living system—where intent is continuously reconciled against the repository state. By treating Architecture-as-Code, governance evolves from a periodic, manual review process into a continuous, reproducible operational feedback loop that guarantees alignment while preserving auditability, replayability, and governance trust.

docs.title: The CAS Approach
docs.text: CAS operationalises architecture governance by establishing a governance aware operational intelligence system capable of continuously reconciling operational reality against architectural intent. At its core, it relies on auditable capability extraction—analysing repository evolution to derive normalised operational capabilities without relying on stochastic governance decisions. Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) serve as the single, machine-readable source of truth, ensuring that governance remains reproducible, auditable, and operationally trustworthy. CAS also establishes governance aware operational workflows for both engineering teams and coding agents, enabling architecture intent to participate directly in the software construction process itself. This operational model establishes the foundation for governance aware coding agent collaboration, where governed operational foundations participate directly in automated software construction workflows. Through CAS Skills, specification-driven development workflows, operational onboarding contracts, and governance aware CI validation, the system prevents significant categories of architectural drift before they materialise while still continuously detecting and correcting what escapes those preventive boundaries. Through continuous operational feedback loops, the system automatically detects structural anomalies, governance drift, and operational capability evolution, empowering architects to manage governance through enablement and automation rather than manual constraint.

docs.title: Operational Outcomes
docs.text: The implementation of CAS fundamentally reduces architectural drift by combining preventive governance mechanisms with continuous operational visibility into the system's structural integrity. This approach increases governance scalability, allowing small architecture teams to oversee massive transformation initiatives safely. By establishing reproducible feedback loops and mandatory architectural guardrails, CAS improves the alignment between executive strategy, engineering delivery, and coding agent execution, ensuring that continuous transformation remains operationally sustainable, governance aware, and architecturally coherent.

docs.title: Broader Implications
docs.text: CAS represents a necessary maturity evolution in how enterprise architecture operates. It signals the transition from architecture as a passive recording function toward architecture as a continuous operational governance system. This operational governance integration demonstrates that complex governance can be operationalised through reproducible intelligence, continuous feedback loops, and governance aware automation without sacrificing strategic optionality or operational safety. By combining governed operational foundations with automated operational interpretation, CAS establishes the foundation for scalable Governance-as-Code in increasingly automated engineering ecosystems. Ultimately, it provides the operational infrastructure required for sustainable enterprise transformation in an era of growing technological and organisational complexity.

docs.title: Related Narrative
docs.text: The operational implications of governance aware software construction become even more significant in highly automated delivery environments where coding agents actively participate in implementation workflows. The companion narrative Governance Aware Coding Agent Collaboration expands on how CAS establishes governed operational foundations, preventive operational controls, and continuous governance reconciliation mechanisms for scalable coding agent ecosystems.

docs.title: Closing Reflection
docs.text: Architecture should never be an isolated review exercise; it must become an active operational capability that participates directly in software delivery. By shifting governance left into the software construction process itself while continuously reconciling repository evolution against architectural intent, CAS closes the gap between strategic direction and engineering reality. The Continuous Architecture System demonstrates that true operational sustainability emerges when architecture evolves from static documentation into a living, measurable, governance aware operational system capable of both preventing and correcting architectural entropy continuously.

docs.title: The Emerging Challenge
docs.text:
Coding agents are rapidly transforming how software is created. By automating implementation tasks, accelerating delivery cycles, and reducing operational friction, these systems significantly increase engineering throughput. However, most organisations are integrating coding agents into delivery environments without equivalent evolution in governance mechanisms.

The result is a dangerous asymmetry: software construction accelerates while architectural governance remains largely manual, reactive, and disconnected from implementation reality.

Without operational governance boundaries, coding agents can unintentionally amplify:

  • architectural drift
  • implementation inconsistency
  • undocumented operational behaviour
  • governance bypass
  • repository entropy
  • uncontrolled technology proliferation

The core issue is not that coding agents are unreliable. The issue is that modern delivery systems increasingly allow implementation decisions to occur outside architecture aware operational constraints.

docs.title: Why Prompt-Driven Governance Fails
docs.text:
Most current approaches to coding agent governance rely heavily on:

  • prompt engineering
  • isolated instruction files
  • static documentation
  • human review checkpoints
  • conversational memory

These mechanisms are insufficient for scalable governance because they remain fundamentally non-operational. Prompts and instructions alone cannot guarantee that architectural intent continuously participates in the software construction lifecycle.

As repositories evolve, prompts become fragmented, operational expectations diverge across teams, and governance consistency deteriorates. The problem compounds further in multi agent environments where different tools interpret guidance differently and operate with varying behavioural assumptions.

Traditional governance mechanisms also operate too late. By the time architecture reviews or manual validations occur, architectural entropy has already entered the repository.

docs.title: The CAS Insight
docs.text:
The critical insight behind CAS is that coding agents should not operate autonomously outside governance boundaries. Instead, architecture intent must become an active participant in software construction itself.

CAS treats coding agent collaboration as an operational governance problem rather than merely an automation problem.

This shifts governance from:

  • reactive review
  • post-implementation correction
  • documentation reconciliation

toward:

  • preventive operational guidance
  • governed implementation workflows
  • governed architectural boundaries
  • continuous operational validation

In this model, coding agents do not simply consume prompts. They operate inside governance aware software construction workflows that continuously reconcile repository evolution against architectural intent.

docs.title: The CAS Approach
docs.text: CAS operationalises governance aware coding agent collaboration through a layered governance model that combines preventive and corrective operational controls.

docs.title: Preventive Governance
docs.text:
Preventive governance mechanisms establish architectural boundaries before implementation divergence occurs.

These mechanisms include:

  • governance aware onboarding packages
  • operational guidance contracts (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md)
  • CAS Skills
  • specification-driven development workflows
  • mandatory architectural sequencing
  • governance aware CI validation
  • operational workflow enforcement

This allows architecture intent to participate directly in the implementation lifecycle from the moment software construction begins.

docs.title: Corrective Governance
docs.text:
Corrective governance mechanisms continuously monitor repository evolution to detect architectural drift that still emerges during delivery.

These workflows include:

  • auditable capability extraction
  • governance drift analysis
  • steering projection workflows
  • operational capability lineage
  • evaluation and validation workflows
  • architecture aware operational reconciliation

Together, these capabilities create continuous governance feedback loops capable of scaling alongside highly automated delivery systems.

docs.title: Auditable Governance Boundaries
docs.text:
A foundational CAS principle is that governance authority must remain reproducible, auditable, and operationally trustworthy.

CAS intentionally separates:

  • auditable governance truth from:
  • semantic operational interpretation

Repository evolution, architectural capability extraction, governance lineage, and operational boundaries remain reproducible and replayable. Semantic reasoning augments governance interpretation but never replaces authoritative governance evidence.

This distinction is critical for ensuring:

  • governance trust
  • operational safety
  • auditability
  • CI/CD enforcement
  • reproducibility
  • scalable enterprise adoption

Rather than creating autonomous governance systems, CAS establishes governance aware operational infrastructure that safely constrains automation inside architecture aligned delivery boundaries.

docs.title: Operational Outcomes
docs.text:
By embedding governance directly into coding agent workflows, CAS transforms software construction from an architecture-blind acceleration mechanism into a governance aware operational system.

The result is:

  • reduced architectural entropy
  • improved implementation consistency
  • scalable coding agent collaboration
  • lower governance friction
  • safer delivery acceleration
  • architecture aware automation
  • continuously aligned repository evolution

Most importantly, CAS enables organisations to scale coding agent adoption without sacrificing architectural coherence, governance integrity, or operational trust.

docs.title: Broader Implications
docs.text:
Governance aware coding agent collaboration represents a necessary evolution in enterprise software delivery. As coding agents increasingly participate in implementation workflows, governance can no longer remain external to the software construction lifecycle.

CAS demonstrates that architecture governance can evolve from passive oversight into an active operational capability that continuously shapes how software is created.

By combining governed operational foundations with governance aware automation, CAS establishes the foundation for scalable, architecture aligned software construction in increasingly automated engineering ecosystems.

The long-term implication is not simply better documentation or safer automation. It is the emergence of governed software construction systems where architecture intent continuously participates in delivery itself.

docs.title: Closing Reflection
docs.text:
Coding agents will fundamentally reshape software engineering. The critical challenge is not whether organisations adopt these systems, but whether governance evolves quickly enough to participate meaningfully in increasingly automated delivery environments.

CAS proposes that the future of architecture governance lies not in restricting automation, but in embedding auditable governance intelligence directly into software construction workflows themselves.

When architecture becomes an active operational participant rather than a passive review function, automation and governance no longer compete. They reinforce each other continuously.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Continuous Architecture System (CAS) operates through structured, goal-oriented orchestration flows. Each flow represents a specific architectural or governance objective, executed via the cas CLI. This document provides a comprehensive reference for each flow, its purpose, and how to execute it.

docs.title: 1. Orchestration Flow (orchestration-flow)
docs.text:
The primary pipeline for the CAS lifecycle. It transforms governance rules and architecture work into a system-wide evolution map and updated architectural intent.

  • Objective: Synchronize Intended Architecture with Actual Architecture.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → AEM Generator → Alignment Engine → AID Generator.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run orchestration-flow --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 2. Governance Validator (governance-validator)
docs.text:
Automates the structural and integrity checks of the knowledge layer. This flow acts as the primary quality gate in CI/CD.

  • Objective: Ensure structural validity, traceability, and lifecycle compliance of all knowledge artifacts.
  • Key Steps: Governance Validator.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run governance-validator --project <name>
    (Note: Can also be run via uv run cas governance validate)

docs.title: 3. Continuous Architecture Loop (continuous-architecture-loop)
docs.text:
Combines the main synchronization pipeline with immediate structural validation in a single execution flow.

  • Objective: Perform end-to-end synchronization and validate structural integrity.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → AEM Generator → Alignment Engine → AID Generator → Governance Validator.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run continuous-architecture-loop --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 4. Baseline Discovery (discovery-flow)
docs.text:
Forensically maps the initial state of an existing project. This is the first flow executed when onboarding a new repository.

  • Objective: Establish the "Actual State" baseline.
  • Key Steps: Baseline Discovery → Rules Context Loader → Conversation to AW → AEM Generator → Alignment Engine → AID Generator.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run discovery-flow --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 5. Steering Projection (steering-projection-flow)
docs.text:
Generates actionable steering proposals to resolve architectural drift identified by the alignment engine.

  • Objective: Propose corrections to keep the codebase aligned with architectural intent.
  • Key Steps: Steering Projection.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run steering-projection-flow --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 6. Architecture Work Assessment (assessment-flow)
docs.text:
Assesses implementation coverage of architecture work items against active capabilities and recommends lifecycle state transitions.

  • Objective: Evaluate alignment evidence and suggest lifecycle status promotions.
  • Key Steps: Governance Context Builder → Architecture Work Assessment.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run assessment-flow --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 7. Roadmap Bootstrap (roadmap-bootstrap-flow)
docs.text:
Initializes or synchronizes a project's product roadmap, initiatives, and items with GitHub Projects.

  • Objective: Load and validate roadmap definitions to build an operational backlog on GitHub.
  • Key Steps: Roadmap Bootstrap.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run roadmap-bootstrap-flow --project <name>

docs.title: 8. Conversation to AW (conversation-to-aw)
docs.text:
Translates unstructured chat history or interview transcripts into structured architecture work artifacts.

  • Objective: Ingest discussions into the architecture work log.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Conversation to AW.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run conversation-to-aw --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 9. Discovery to AW (discovery-to-aw)
docs.text:
Converts baseline discovery reports and scan results into structured architecture work artifacts.

  • Objective: Ingest discovered artifacts into the architecture work log.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Discovery to AW.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run discovery-to-aw --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 10. Vision to AW (vision-to-aw)
docs.text:
Converts high-level strategy and vision documentation into structured architecture work.

  • Objective: Translate strategic goals into actionable architecture work.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Vision to AW.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run vision-to-aw --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 11. Current Architecture State (current-architecture-state-generator)
docs.text:
Synthesizes the overall state of the system architecture from various input sources to maintain a comprehensive architectural viewpoint.

  • Objective: Generate a consolidated viewpoint of the current system state.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Current Architecture State Generator.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run current-architecture-state-generator --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 12. Signal to Pattern (signal-to-pattern-proposals)
docs.text:
Analyzes architectural signals and learnings to identify emerging concepts.

  • Objective: Discover new candidate patterns from operational evidence.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Signal to Pattern Proposals.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run signal-to-pattern-proposals --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 13. Pattern Scope Classifier (pattern-scope-classifier)
docs.text:
Determines the architectural scope (Global vs. Project) of proposed patterns.

  • Objective: Assign appropriate governance boundaries to emerging concepts.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Pattern Scope Classifier.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run pattern-scope-classifier --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 14. Pattern Promotion (pattern-promotion-workflow)
docs.text:
Evaluates scoped proposals against promotion criteria to generate formal recommendations.

  • Objective: Filter emerging concepts into "Recommended" candidates for institutionalization.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Pattern Promotion Workflow.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run pattern-promotion-workflow --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 15. Promotion Decision Capture (promotion-decision-capture)
docs.text:
Captures the human architect's decision on a system-recommended pattern promotion.

  • Objective: Provide the formal human-in-the-loop gate for pattern adoption.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Promotion Decision Capture.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run promotion-decision-capture --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 16. Promotion to ADR (promotion-to-decision-records)
docs.text:
Transforms accepted promotion decisions into formal Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).

  • Objective: Formalize architectural decisions into the Single Source of Truth.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Promotion to Decision Records.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run promotion-to-decision-records --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: 17. Approved ADR to Pattern (approved-adr-to-pattern)
docs.text:
Converts forum-approved ADRs into institutionalised Pattern artifacts.

  • Objective: Complete the lifecycle by establishing new architectural standards.
  • Key Steps: Rules Context Loader → Approved ADR to Pattern.
  • CLI Execution: 
    uv run cas run approved-adr-to-pattern --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: Platform Operations & Utility Commands
docs.text: Beyond reasoning and sync flows, the cas CLI provides various commands for workspace setup, steering section operations, trace evaluations, and governance decisions.

docs.title: 1. Workspace Initialization (init-workspace)
docs.text:
Initializes or attaches to a CAS knowledge workspace, mapping a project to a shared local or remote storage directory. - Objective: Attach/bootstrap workspace paths and configure standard knowledge providers. - CLI Execution: 

uv run cas init-workspace --project <name> [--workspace-root <path>] [--provider <provider>] [--force]

docs.title: 2. Platform Bootstrap (bootstrap)
docs.text:
Sets up the initial CAS governance substrate, CI workflow directories, and configuration settings in a new repository. - Objective: Install the baseline CAS governance files and configurations. - CLI Execution: 

uv run cas bootstrap [target_directory] [--force] [--minimal] [--no-ci]

docs.title: 3. Governance Operations (governance)
docs.text:
Provides administrative operations for validating, merging, and transitioning the state of governed artifacts. - Actions: - Validate (validate): Runs structural and schema validation checks (alias for governance-validator flow). 

uv run cas governance validate --project <name> [--provider <provider>]
- Assess (assess): Evaluates implementation coverage of Architecture Work (alias for assessment-flow flow). 
uv run cas governance assess --project <name> [--provider <provider>]
- Conflict Resolver (resolve-conflicts): Discovers git conflict markers within the knowledge layer (.yaml, .json, .md) and automatically resolves them using the LLM-powered Agentic Merger. 
uv run cas governance resolve-conflicts --project <name> [--provider <provider>]
- Action Service (approve / reject / defer / reopen): Transitions the status of a specific governed artifact (promotion decisions, ADRs, exceptions, architecture work items) with a provided justification. 
uv run cas governance approve <artifact_id> --rationale <text> --project <name>

docs.title: 4. Steering Operations (steering)
docs.text:
Manages capability inventories and applies proposed steering projections to align the codebase. - Actions: - Validate (validate): Verifies that managed steering sections inside documents are intact and structurally valid. 

uv run cas steering validate [--managed-sections-only]
- Apply (apply): Parses and applies proposed capability change replacements (from frontmatter proposals) directly into target source files. 
uv run cas steering apply --projection <projection_id_or_path> [--dry-run]
- Bootstrap (bootstrap): Performs a one-time baseline git reference scan to bootstrap the Runtime Capability Inventory. 
uv run cas steering bootstrap --project <name> [--baseline-ref <hash>]

docs.title: 5. Governance Dashboard (dashboard)
docs.text:
Renders and prints a summary of the project's architectural compliance and health metrics in markdown or json formats. - Objective: Inspect the local compliance state of the project. - CLI Execution: 

uv run cas dashboard --project <name> [--format markdown|json]

docs.title: 6. Trace Evaluation (evaluate)
docs.text:
Runs LLM-powered quality evaluations on trace files generated by prior reasoning runs to score response quality and check rules alignment. - Objective: Run automated eval criteria against execution history logs. - CLI Execution: 

uv run cas evaluate <trace_id_prefix> --project <name> --provider <provider>

docs.title: Operational Summary
docs.text:
• Idempotency: All CAS flows are designed to be idempotent; running them multiple times against the same input will yield consistent, versioned artifacts.
  • Human-in-the-Loop: While flows automate the "Detect" and "Propose" stages, the "Decide" stage (Action Framework) remains an explicit human-driven gate.
  • Telemetry: Every execution generates a trace log in knowledge/runtime/traces/, enabling continuous evaluation of orchestration quality.

docs.title: The Separation of State and Action
docs.text:
In the early stages of CAS, governance state transitions (like approving an ADR) required manually editing the YAML frontmatter of the artifact file. While functionally correct, this approach conflated the artifact's State with the Action of changing it, leading to operational friction as governance volume grew.

The Governance Action Framework solves this by enforcing a strict architectural principle: Artifacts store state. Actions change state. The Engine governs transitions.

docs.title: The Action Engine
docs.text:
The GovernanceActionEngine is the centralized authority for all governance state changes. It operates on a Transition Registry that defines valid state machines for each artifact type.

For example, a Promotion Decision can transition from pending to accepted, rejected, or deferred. An attempt to transition directly from deferred to accepted will be rejected by the engine.

This engine is exposed through the CAS CLI: 

cas governance approve <artifact-id>
cas governance reject <artifact-id> --rationale "Missing evidence"

docs.title: Immutable Audit Trails
docs.text:
Accountability requires traceability. Every successful state transition executed by the engine generates a formal GovernanceAction audit record.

These records are immutable YAML files stored in knowledge/global/governance/actions/. They capture: - The exact transition (e.g., pending -> accepted) - The target artifact - The executing user identity - The cryptographic timestamp - Any provided rationale

docs.title: Future-Proofing
docs.text: By routing all state changes through a single, registry-driven engine, CAS is prepared for future capabilities such as UI-based "one-click" approvals in the Governance Portal or autonomous AI-driven governance decisions. All interfaces will delegate to the Action Engine, guaranteeing consistent validation and auditing.

docs.title: Why Compliance Exists
docs.text: The Continuous Architecture System (CAS) ensures that architecture evolves with integrity. While Governance Integrity (Sprint 1) focuses on structural validity and Governance Intelligence (Sprint 2) provides visibility, Governance Compliance establishes accountability. It ensures that the governance rules defined by the collective are actively followed and that deviations are explicitly managed.

docs.title: How Compliance Works
docs.text: Compliance in CAS is metadata-driven. We don't hardcode rigid policies in Python; instead, we treat our Governance Rules as the authoritative source of truth for both human guidance and automated evaluation.

docs.title: Rule-Based Model
docs.text:
A rule participates in compliance evaluation if it contains the following frontmatter:

compliance:
  enabled: true
  validation_type: "status_check"
  target: "adrs"
  field: "governance.forum_status"
  expected: "accepted"
  severity: "error"
  recommendation: "Submit for forum review"

The Compliance Engine discovers these enabled rules and evaluates them against the knowledge layer during every validation run.

docs.title: Exception Model
docs.text:
We recognize that architecture is often about managing technical debt and navigating pragmatism. The Compliance Exception model allows architects to explicitly accept a non-compliant state for a specific period.

Exceptions are formal governance artifacts: - Location: knowledge/global/governance/exceptions/ - Governance: Requires rationale, approver, and an expiry date.

Active exceptions suppress CI/CD failures, ensuring the pipeline remains green for accepted debt while keeping that debt highly visible in compliance dashboards.

docs.title: Compliance Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Rule Definition: A governance rule is established or updated with compliance metadata.
  2. Evaluation: The Compliance Engine runs (locally or in CI/CD).
  3. Detection: Violations are identified and categorized (error, warning, info).
  4. Action:
    • Green: Compliant.
    • Block: Violations (errors) without exceptions fail the build.
    • Exception: Architect records a formal exception to suppress the build.
    • Resolution: Artifact is updated to meet the rule, and the exception is retired.

docs.title: Accountability, Not Bottlenecks
docs.text: The goal of Governance Compliance is to identify gaps early. It provides the data necessary for the Governance Forum to make informed decisions about where to invest in alignment and where to grant flexibility, ensuring that the system's "Actual Architecture" stays aligned with its "Intended Architecture."

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document explains the governance foundation of the Continuous Architecture System (CAS).

It describes why governance exists, the capabilities currently implemented, and how governance artifacts evolve from architectural signals into institutionalized patterns.

This is a platform narrative rather than an implementation specification.

docs.title: Why Governance Exists
docs.text:
Traditional architecture governance is often periodic, manual, and disconnected from delivery.

Architecture reviews happen after decisions have already been made, creating delays, inconsistent decision-making, and limited organizational learning.

CAS takes a different approach.

Governance is treated as a continuous capability embedded into the architecture lifecycle.

Rather than governing only completed solutions, CAS governs the evolution of architectural knowledge itself.

The objective is to continuously transform:

text Signals ↓ Insights ↓ Patterns ↓ Institutional Knowledge

while preserving traceability, evidence, and architectural intent.

docs.title: Governance Principles
docs.text: The governance foundation is built upon the following principles.

docs.title: Governance as a Continuous Capability
docs.text:
Governance is not a stage.

Governance is an ongoing activity operating throughout the architecture lifecycle.

Architectural learning continuously feeds governance decisions.

Governance decisions continuously influence future architectural work.

docs.title: Traceability First
docs.text:
Every governance artifact must be traceable.

Governance decisions should never appear without supporting evidence and lineage.

CAS therefore maintains explicit relationships between:

text Pattern Proposal ↓ Promotion Recommendation ↓ Promotion Decision ↓ Architecture Decision Record ↓ Institutionalized Pattern

This lineage forms the governance chain.

docs.title: Human Decision Authority
docs.text:
CAS supports governance decisions but does not replace them.

The platform may:

  • identify patterns
  • recommend promotion
  • generate governance artifacts
  • validate governance integrity

The platform does not:

  • approve patterns
  • reject patterns
  • override governance decisions

Architectural authority remains with architects and governance forums.

The governing principle is:

text System validates process. Architect makes decisions.

docs.title: Governance as Code
docs.text:
Governance should be executable.

Governance artifacts are represented as structured knowledge objects.

Governance workflows generate governance artifacts.

Governance validation is automated through CI/CD.

This enables governance to become observable, repeatable, and enforceable.

docs.title: Governance Lifecycle
docs.text:
The governance lifecycle institutionalizes architectural learning.

text Pattern Proposal ↓ Promotion Recommendation ↓ Promotion Decision ↓ Architecture Decision Record (ADR) ↓ Governance Forum Review ↓ Institutionalized Pattern

Each stage produces explicit governance artifacts.

docs.title: Pattern Proposal
docs.text:
Pattern proposals capture recurring architectural observations.

They represent candidate patterns that may become institutional knowledge.

A proposal does not imply approval.

A proposal indicates:

text This observation appears significant enough to warrant governance review.

docs.title: Promotion Recommendation
docs.text:
Promotion recommendations assess whether a proposed pattern should progress toward institutionalization.

Recommendations evaluate:

  • significance
  • recurrence
  • reusability
  • evidence quality
  • strategic alignment

Recommendations support decision making.

They do not make decisions.

docs.title: Promotion Decision
docs.text:
Promotion decisions capture architectural intent.

The responsible architect records whether the pattern should:

text Promote Defer Reject

A promotion decision creates governance accountability.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
docs.text:
An ADR formalizes governance intent.

The ADR captures:

  • decision
  • rationale
  • context
  • consequences
  • governance traceability

The ADR becomes the primary governance artifact reviewed by the Architecture Forum.

docs.title: Governance Forum Review
docs.text:
Governance Forums review ADRs.

Forums may:

text Approve Reject Approve with Conditions Defer

The review outcome is recorded directly within the ADR.

Governance review represents the formal institutionalization gate.

docs.title: Institutionalized Pattern
docs.text:
Approved ADRs become institutionalized patterns.

Patterns represent reusable architectural knowledge.

Patterns are no longer project-specific observations.

They become part of the CAS knowledge base.

Institutionalized patterns influence:

  • future architecture work
  • onboarding workflows
  • governance validation
  • alignment reviews

docs.title: Governance Artifacts
docs.text: The governance foundation introduces several artifact types.

docs.title: Pattern Proposal
docs.text: Captures a candidate architectural pattern.

docs.title: Promotion Recommendation
docs.text: Captures evidence-based promotion guidance.

docs.title: Promotion Decision
docs.text: Captures architect intent regarding promotion.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Record
docs.text: Captures governance rationale and forum review outcomes.

docs.title: Pattern
docs.text: Captures institutionalized architectural knowledge.

docs.title: Governance Portal
docs.text:
The Governance Portal provides operational visibility of governance state.

The Portal is a projection layer.

It visualizes governance artifacts without becoming the source of truth.

The Portal exposes:

text Pattern Proposals Promotion Recommendations Promotion Decisions ADRs Pending Review Approved ADRs Institutionalized Patterns

The Portal enables architects to navigate governance lineage and monitor governance health.

docs.title: Governance CI/CD
docs.text:
Governance validation is automated.

The Governance Validator continuously verifies:

text Schema Integrity Traceability Integrity Lifecycle Integrity Governance State Integrity

Validation occurs both locally and within CI/CD pipelines.

Governance automation validates process integrity.

Governance automation does not replace architectural judgement.

Planned areas include:

docs.title: Governance Intelligence
docs.text:
Provide operational governance insights, and relies on"

  • Governance Metrics

Examples:

docs.title: Governance Compliance
docs.text:
Provide automated compliance validation.

Examples:

  • pattern compliance
  • governance policy validation
  • architectural conformance checks

docs.title: Governance Drift Detection
docs.text:
Identify divergence between institutionalized patterns and implementation reality.

Examples:

  • pattern adoption monitoring
  • architecture drift detection
  • governance risk indicators

docs.title: Architectural Outcome
docs.text:
The governance foundation transforms governance from a periodic review activity into a continuous architectural capability.

CAS continuously converts architectural learning into institutional knowledge while preserving evidence, traceability, and human decision authority.

The resulting governance model combines:

text Governance Generation + Governance Visibility + Governance Validation

to create an operational governance capability embedded within the architecture lifecycle.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text: Traditional enterprise architecture relies heavily on static documentation to govern complex systems. While these artifacts capture initial strategic intent, they are inherently disconnected from the engineering reality. As systems evolve, a critical gap forms between the documented architecture and the actual implementation, leading to severe documentation drift and a loss of alignment. The fundamental problem is that static governance mechanisms cannot scale to meet the demands of modern delivery velocity without introducing unacceptable friction.

docs.title: Why Traditional Governance Breaks
docs.text: Architecture governance typically degrades not because of engineering failure, but due to systemic operational limitations. Manual review processes and point-in-time assessments are fundamentally incompatible with continuous delivery and agile execution. As an organisation scales, the administrative burden of maintaining architectural alignment across disconnected teams becomes unsustainable. This friction inevitably leads to architectural drift, where the system's operational reality diverges from strategic intent, creating hidden technical debt and operational risk.

docs.title: Shift-Left Governance
docs.text:
Traditional governance mechanisms operate too late in the delivery lifecycle, relying on post-implementation reviews, documentation reconciliation, and periodic oversight to detect architectural divergence. CAS shifts architecture governance directly into the software construction process itself, establishing preventive operational guardrails that guide implementation from the moment code is created while continuously detecting and correcting what still escapes those boundaries.

This creates a dual-governance operational model:

  • Preventive Governance — Governance aware onboarding, CAS Skills, coding agent operational guidance, specification-driven development workflows, and CI validation establish architectural boundaries before implementation diverges.
  • Corrective Governance — Continuous governance workflows, capability extraction, steering projection, evaluation, and operational reconciliation detect and correct architectural drift that still emerges during system evolution.

By embedding governance directly into software construction workflows, CAS transforms architecture from a passive review function into an active operational capability that continuously shapes repository evolution in real time. This governance aware software construction model becomes increasingly critical in environments where coding agents actively participate in delivery workflows.

docs.title: The Architectural Insight
docs.text: The resolution to this drift lies in shifting the paradigm from static documentation and reactive governance toward operational intelligence embedded directly into the software construction lifecycle. The core insight behind the Continuous Architecture System (CAS) is that architecture must operate as a living system—where intent is continuously reconciled against the repository state. By treating Architecture-as-Code, governance evolves from a periodic, manual review process into a continuous, reproducible operational feedback loop that guarantees alignment while preserving auditability, replayability, and governance trust.

docs.title: The CAS Approach
docs.text: CAS operationalises architecture governance by establishing a governance aware operational intelligence system capable of continuously reconciling operational reality against architectural intent. At its core, it relies on auditable capability extraction—analysing repository evolution to derive normalised operational capabilities without relying on stochastic governance decisions. Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) serve as the single, machine-readable source of truth, ensuring that governance remains reproducible, auditable, and operationally trustworthy. CAS also establishes governance aware operational workflows for both engineering teams and coding agents, enabling architecture intent to participate directly in the software construction process itself. This operational model establishes the foundation for governance aware coding agent collaboration, where governed operational foundations participate directly in automated software construction workflows. Through CAS Skills, specification-driven development workflows, operational onboarding contracts, and governance aware CI validation, the system prevents significant categories of architectural drift before they materialise while still continuously detecting and correcting what escapes those preventive boundaries. Through continuous operational feedback loops, the system automatically detects structural anomalies, governance drift, and operational capability evolution, empowering architects to manage governance through enablement and automation rather than manual constraint.

docs.title: Operational Outcomes
docs.text: The implementation of CAS fundamentally reduces architectural drift by combining preventive governance mechanisms with continuous operational visibility into the system's structural integrity. This approach increases governance scalability, allowing small architecture teams to oversee massive transformation initiatives safely. By establishing reproducible feedback loops and mandatory architectural guardrails, CAS improves the alignment between executive strategy, engineering delivery, and coding agent execution, ensuring that continuous transformation remains operationally sustainable, governance aware, and architecturally coherent.

docs.title: Broader Implications
docs.text: CAS represents a necessary maturity evolution in how enterprise architecture operates. It signals the transition from architecture as a passive recording function toward architecture as a continuous operational governance system. This operational governance integration demonstrates that complex governance can be operationalised through reproducible intelligence, continuous feedback loops, and governance aware automation without sacrificing strategic optionality or operational safety. By combining governed operational foundations with automated operational interpretation, CAS establishes the foundation for scalable Governance-as-Code in increasingly automated engineering ecosystems. Ultimately, it provides the operational infrastructure required for sustainable enterprise transformation in an era of growing technological and organisational complexity.

docs.title: Related Narrative
docs.text: The operational implications of governance aware software construction become even more significant in highly automated delivery environments where coding agents actively participate in implementation workflows. The companion narrative Governance Aware Coding Agent Collaboration expands on how CAS establishes governed operational foundations, preventive operational controls, and continuous governance reconciliation mechanisms for scalable coding agent ecosystems.

docs.title: Closing Reflection
docs.text: Architecture should never be an isolated review exercise; it must become an active operational capability that participates directly in software delivery. By shifting governance left into the software construction process itself while continuously reconciling repository evolution against architectural intent, CAS closes the gap between strategic direction and engineering reality. The Continuous Architecture System demonstrates that true operational sustainability emerges when architecture evolves from static documentation into a living, measurable, governance aware operational system capable of both preventing and correcting architectural entropy continuously.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Implement the Governance Health and Intelligence Dashboard using a layered architecture and a deterministic heuristic health model.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Source: specs/030-governance-health-intelligence-dashboard/spec.md
  • Decision classification: system

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The CAS portal lacks a central landing experience that synthesizes governance health. Users must read individual ADRs, Architecture Work items, and Alignment Reports to understand the system state, which is inefficient for high-level monitoring and risk identification.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
1. Layered Decoupling: Separating data access (data_access.py), health logic (health_model.py), and the web interface ensures the health engine can be tested independently of the UI.
  2. Heuristic Model (Phase 1): Using simple, transparent heuristics (e.g., Red status if high-severity findings exist) ensures trust and allows for incremental refinement.
  3. Read-Only Intelligence: The dashboard serves as a consumption layer. It derives insights but never becomes a new source of truth, preserving the ADR as the authoritative record.
  4. Information Scent: Providing summaries with direct links to artifacts (Traceability) ensures users can verify insights without friction.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text:
• Implement the cas_runner/dashboard/ module structure.
  • Define specific heuristic triggers for Green/Amber/Red states in the health model.
  • Replace the portal homepage with the synthesized dashboard view.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt the Runtime Capability Inventory (inventory.yaml) as the project-specific representation of current implemented capabilities. It is initialized via a one-time bootstrap script (scanning the repository using a git diff against the empty tree hash) and kept up-to-date incrementally during Capability Extraction.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Source: specs/062-cas-runtime-capability-bootstrap/spec.md
  • Decision classification: system

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Downstream governance workflows like Architecture Work Assessment and Governance Context Builder require a complete view of currently implemented runtime capabilities. Scraping raw commit deltas directly is insufficient because deltas only describe recent changes, meaning pre-existing or unchanged capabilities are omitted.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
1. State vs Evolution Separation: Separation of concerns between change extraction (deltas) and current state tracking (inventory).
  2. Deterministic Bootstrapping: Reuses the git-extractor diff mechanism against the empty tree hash 4b825dc642cb6eb9a0f94140d12a1d9a3435b1d57, guaranteeing identical parsing rules to standard commits.
  3. Traceability Preservation: Retired capabilities are flagged as retired instead of deleted, preserving historical references.
  4. Direct Consumers: Allows Context Builder to load all capability evidence instantly from one single file instead of performing costly codebase scans.

docs.title: ADR-067: Target Project Evidence Isolation & Positive Boundary Containment
ADR-067: Target Project Evidence Isolation & Positive Boundary Containment
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
During the onboarding diagnostic of an external project (EA4ALL), CAS generated architectural baselines and evolution maps that predominantly described the CAS platform implementation engine (ideas-to-life-cas) rather than the target project being analyzed (ea4all). The diagnostic identified that:

  1. Foundational asset loading (load_foundational_assets) loaded engine source files (src/**/*.md) relative to process CWD and global CAS platform ADRs into the target project evidence set.
  2. Baseline discovery extracted historical dates (such as 2024-05-22 from CAS engine ADRs) into target project baseline artifacts.
  3. CLI commands and portal preprocessors defaulted to ideas-to-life-cas identity.

Initial remediation proposals considered creating an accumulating list of path-specific negative exclusions (such as excluding src/**/*.md, portal/**, and knowledge/**). However, negative path filtering is fragile, non-scalable, and breaks when new engine directories are introduced.

docs.title: Architectural Invariant
docs.text: "Target Project Repository Root defines Project Evidence."

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Adopt structural Positive Boundary Containment for target project evidence isolation across the Continuous Architecture System (CAS):

  1. TargetProjectContext Prerequisites: Prior to evidence discovery, every CAS workflow execution MUST establish an authoritative TargetProjectContext containing, at minimum:
  2. project_id (canonical slug)
  3. project_root (absolute path to project root)

  4. evidence_root (absolute path to target project evidence root)

  5. Positive Boundary Containment: Foundational project evidence discovery MUST operate strictly within the evidence_root established by TargetProjectContext (which resolves to the target project's repository root or an explicitly defined evidence path beneath it). The target project’s repository root defines the maximum project-evidence boundary; evidence_root defines the authoritative evidence scope within that boundary.

  6. No Accumulating Negative Exclusion Lists: Files outside evidence_root (including CAS engine code, platform docs, workflow implementations, templates, and portal assets) are excluded structurally by boundary containment. CAS MUST NOT rely on path-specific negative exclusion rules (such as src/**/*.md or portal/**).

  7. Symmetric Execution Rules: The exact same foundational loader implementation and boundary rules apply whether analyzing the CAS platform itself (project_id: ideas-to-life-cas) or an external target project (project_id: ea4all).

  8. Explicit Reference Mechanisms for Shared Context: Shared or cross-project CAS knowledge MUST be accessed through explicit, declared reference mechanisms rather than being automatically ingested into a project's foundational evidence bundle.

  9. Dynamic Portal Discovery & Resolution: TargetProjectContext and cas-config.yaml serve as the single source of project identity across CLI, runner, reference resolution, and Portal preprocessing.

docs.title: Alternative 1: Accumulating Negative Path Exclusion Filters (src/**/*.md, portal/**, knowledge/**)
docs.text:
• Pros: Quick to patch in load_foundational_assets().
  • Cons: Fragile, maintenance-heavy, incomplete (fails to catch new engine paths), and breaks symmetry when CAS itself is the target project.
  • Outcome: Rejected.

docs.title: Alternative 2: Textual Prompt Guardrails ("Do not analyze CAS; analyze EA4ALL")
docs.text:
• Pros: Zero code changes to loaders.
  • Cons: Violates NFR-05; non-deterministic, consumes prompt window, fails to prevent upstream context contamination.
  • Outcome: Rejected.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive:
  • Robust, deterministic project isolation grounded in structural filesystem containment.
  • Complete elimination of engine code leaking into external project baselines.
  • Provenance of baseline dates is strictly traceable to target project evidence or current execution temporal context (date.today().isoformat()).
  • Identical loader logic works symmetrically for CAS platform self-analysis and external project analysis.
  • Negative:
  • Requires all CLI entrypoints and runners to construct TargetProjectContext before invoking evidence discovery.
  • Requires cas-config.yaml or explicit --repo-root flags when executing outside a standard project workspace layout.

docs.title: ADR-075: Architecture State Forensic Diagnostic & Baseline Acceptance
ADR-075: Architecture State Forensic Diagnostic & Baseline Acceptance
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Brownfield and evolving codebases often suffer from architectural drift—a gap between documented architectural intent (in READMEs, wikis, or historical ADRs) and actual runtime implementation.

Existing discovery mechanisms in CAS captured high-level conversational summaries and text documents, but lacked fine-grained empirical reconstruction directly from source manifests, workflow configurations, AST symbol graphs, and import dependencies.

Furthermore, automatic mutation of the validated baseline risked poisoning architectural truth with speculative or contradictory representations.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
We adopt the Architecture State Forensic Diagnostic (CAS-ARCH-STATE v0.1) with the following core architectural decisions:

  1. Four-Pillar Architecture State Package: Reconstruction outputs are partitioned into a dedicated structure under knowledge/projects/<project>/architecture-state/:
  2. model/: intermediate architecture-state.yaml and partitioned YAML files (systems.yaml, containers.yaml, components.yaml, dependencies.yaml, flows.yaml, controls.yaml, evidence.yaml).
  3. views/: 5 C4-inspired Markdown views (system-context.md, containers.md, components.md, architecture-flow.md, governance-controls.md).
  4. diagrams/: Mermaid .mmd diagrams for system context and container boundaries.
  5. diagnostic/: Forensic reports (evidence-report.md, contradictions.md, unknowns.md, coverage.md).

  6. ARCHITECTURE.md: Consolidated single-file architectural digest.

  7. Zero Uninvited Root Writes: ARCHITECTURE.md is strictly contained within the knowledge layer by default; it is only mirrored to <target-dir>/ARCHITECTURE.md when the explicit --publish-root flag is supplied.

  8. Standard-Library Python AST Extraction: For Python targets, extraction utilizes Python's built-in ast module to guarantee zero heavy binary dependencies. Polyglot targets utilize regex and manifest parsers.

  9. Non-Blocking Contradiction Auditing: Discrepancies between documented intent and empirical code do not abort execution; conflicting nodes are flagged with status: contradictory and confidence: low, and cataloged in contradictions.md.

  10. Human-in-the-Loop Baseline Promotion Gate: Discovered states remain in status: discovered until an architect explicitly promotes the state via uv run cas state baseline promote --project <project>, freezing a point-in-time snapshot under knowledge/projects/<project>/baseline/.

docs.title: Problem

docs.title: ADR: Adopt Hybrid LLM Gateway Integration
ADR: Adopt Hybrid LLM Gateway Integration
Context
docs.text: The CAS system currently uses a stubbed LLM provider. To support real-world architectural flows, we need to integrate with multiple providers (Gemini, OpenAI, etc.) while ensuring that outputs are machine-readable and system stability is maintained.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We will implement a unified LLM Gateway in src/cas_runner/llm/ that: 1. Defines a provider-agnostic LLMClient protocol. 2. Uses LiteLLM for normalized multi-provider execution. 3. Mandates Pydantic schemas for all reasoning steps. 4. Implements robust JSON extraction to handle model "chatter".

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Pros: Provider agnosticism, strict type safety, reduced boilerplate for adding new models.
  • Cons: Adds litellm and pydantic as core dependencies.
  • Risks: Potential for validation failures if models deviate from complex schemas.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The AEM roadmap included "Pattern Classification Framework" as a NEXT item, but this transition lacked a formal decision record. Without a defined framework, the distinction between core, supporting, and project-specific patterns remains subjective, leading to potential knowledge drift and rule bloating in the global layer.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: A formal classification framework is necessary to: 1. Provide objective criteria for promoting a pattern from project-specific to global scope. 2. Define the precedence and isolation boundaries between global rules and project-level constraints. 3. Ensure that the knowledge layer remains modular and scalable as more projects are added to the CAS. 4. Support the "System Proposes, Architect Decides" rule by providing the architect with a clear classification rubric.

docs.title: Next Step

  • Update the pattern-scope-classifier.v1 prompt to reflect the new framework.
  • Audit existing patterns in knowledge/global/patterns/ against the new criteria.

docs.title: System Evolution
docs.text:
CAS has evolved from a deterministic transformation pipeline into a governed semantic reasoning infrastructure. The system now enforces strict input scoping, two-phase diagram handling, and a proposal-decision separation invariant. Orchestration is driven by a ReasoningExecutionContract that mandates schema validation and separates reasoning from rendering. Governance is centralized via a rules-context-loader and conflict detector, establishing a global > project > prompt precedence hierarchy. Observability is integrated through OTEL-compatible telemetry, capturing reasoning lineage, token economics, and provider behavior. The system operates on a two-phase model: design-time governance (CAS Skills) and runtime orchestration (FlowRunner), ensuring deterministic execution while supporting LLM-backed reasoning steps.

CAS has now entered a measurable architecture cognition phase where orchestration quality, governance reasoning, semantic contracts, prompt lineage, and provider economics are observable and evaluable. The platform is evolving toward a closed Prevent ↔ Detect ↔ Feedback governance loop integrating CAS Skills, orchestration workflows, evaluation harnesses, and future CI/CD audit pipelines. Strategic focus has shifted from foundational orchestration refactoring toward ReasoningOps, GovernanceOps, adaptive orchestration policies, and operational architecture governance.

docs.title: Intent & Direction
docs.text:
CAS is transitioning from an architecture extraction system to an Architecture Intelligence Platform. The vision emphasizes connecting business intent, architecture, code, and decisions through continuous alignment and traceability. Future directions include business layer integration (BRD ingestion), code intelligence for structural analysis, and enterprise ecosystem integration (EAM tools). The system aims to support capability-aware model routing, adaptive reasoning optimization, and an evaluation-driven improvement loop. Human-in-the-loop governance remains core, with automation proposing and architects deciding. Visual interaction layers (AIM) and graph-native knowledge representation are planned for future exploration.

Near-term strategic priorities focus on operationalizing continuous architecture governance through CI/CD-integrated audit workflows, orchestration economics visibility, validation governance telemetry, and lightweight capability-aware routing. Longer-term direction includes GovernanceOps workflows for pattern evolution, governance drift management, architecture intelligence integration across business and code layers, and external validation of CAS as a continuous architecture governance platform.

docs.title: Intent & Direction

The forward trajectory focuses on connecting business intent to architecture and code, enabling continuous alignment between intent (AID) and implementation reality. Future capabilities include cross-project knowledge graphs, interactive architecture intelligence maps, and external ecosystem integration. The vision emphasizes traceability, automated drift detection, and human-governed continuous evolution. Architecture intent artefacts will align with system state rather than merely reflecting it, supporting proactive prevention and detection of architectural drift.

docs.title: System Evolution
docs.text: The system is evolving from a template-driven documentation model to a runtime-active 'Architecture Intelligence Platform'. Key changes include the move to a Decoupled Execution Model where the CAS Runner orchestrates logic-independent workflows. The Architecture Work Registry has been elevated to the authoritative planning source to prevent data loss during artifact regeneration. Governance is shifting toward a 'Continuous Participation' model using automated Detect-Analyse-Execute loops to address the 15:1 velocity bottleneck.

docs.title: Intent & Direction
docs.text: Forward-looking intent focuses on closing the 'Business to Code' loop. The vision establishes 'Architecture Intelligence' as a layer capable of multi-hop lineage analysis via a Knowledge Graph and automated alignment of AID (target) with Code (reality). Future goals include 'Portfolio Intelligence' for cross-project visibility and 'External Ecosystem Integration' to synchronize decisions with EAM tools.

Key structural shifts include the institutionalization of the Architecture Work Registry as the authoritative backlog (resolving planning-state loss) and the decoupling of reasoning logic from orchestration via the Workflow Execution Model. Future goals include cross-project Portfolio Intelligence and an explorable Architecture Knowledge Graph to analyze capability dependencies and decision lineage across the entire enterprise ecosystem.

docs.title: System Evolution
docs.text: The system operations have transitioned from prompt-driven manual governance and static generation into an automated, runtime-native Continuous Architecture Governance platform. The CAS Workflow Execution Model cleanly bifurcates orchestration (FlowRunner) and reasoning (prompts/workflows), reinforced by LiteLLM gateway integration with strict Pydantic schemas. Architectural planning state has been formally decoupled from generated views: the Architecture Work Registry is now the authoritative planning backlog, making the Architecture Evolution Map (AEM) a derived dashboard rather than an independent planning system. Empirical evidence gathering is fortified through ADR-067 (Positive Boundary Containment) and ADR-075 (Forensic Diagnostics), ensuring structural isolation between the target repository and CAS runner internals, backed by human-in-the-loop promotion gates before modifying baseline truth.

docs.title: Intent & Direction
docs.text: Project intent focuses on evolving CAS into an end-to-end Architecture Intelligence Platform connecting Business Intent, Architecture, Code Reality, and Decisions. Forward-looking initiatives target the ingestion of business requirement signals to constrain alignment reasoning, closing the loop between target architectural intent (AID) and implementation reality (Code) via AST structural analysis, and establishing a unified Architecture Knowledge Graph for cross-project dependency and lineage modeling. Operational governance aims to shift from periodic batch reviews to an automated detect-analyse-execute cycle embedded into CI/CD workflows, while preserving human architectural authority for binding decision acceptance.

docs.title: System Evolution
docs.text: The Continuous Architecture System has progressed from a manual script and template scaffolding into a continuous, runtime-native architecture steering platform. FlowRunner executes multi-step declarative workflows configured in steps/registry.py, orchestrated alongside GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines. Core execution decoupling (adr-pattern-cas-decoupled-execution-model) ensures runtime steps remain agnostic to persistence mechanisms via the KnowledgeProvider abstraction (adr-knowledge-repository-abstraction). Boundary containment (adr-067) and empirical AST-based forensic extraction (adr-075) eliminate cross-project leakage and reconstruct empirical system state directly from repository code. Architecture Work is established as the authoritative planning backlog, while the Architecture Evolution Map operates as a derived dashboard aligning target intent with empirical state.

docs.title: Intent & Direction
docs.text: Project vision directs CAS to expand beyond technical code alignment into an end-to-end Architecture Intelligence Platform connecting Business Intent, Architecture, Code, and Decisions. Near-term focus prioritizes formalizing the Business Intent artifact schema to ingest strategic requirements directly into the Alignment Engine, preventing strategic drift before pull requests are committed. Medium-term initiatives focus on closing the Detect-Analyse-Execute loop through automated CI-triggered remediation signals and building out a multi-hop Architecture Knowledge Graph to evaluate cross-project dependency impacts.
