docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Pure Health Evaluator (src/cas_runner/dashboard/health_model.py): Hosts pure functions including calculate_health and get_health_reasons. Accepts strongly typed metrics models and yields health classification outcomes without external dependencies.
  • Health Status Value Model (src/cas_runner/dashboard/health_model.py): Encapsulates categorical health classifications (e.g., HealthStatus enum) and diagnostic reason payloads.
  • Metrics Collector Shell (src/cas_runner/dashboard/): Manages operational side effects, querying external telemetry sources or data stores to assemble immutable inputs before triggering domain evaluation.

docs.title: Technology choices
docs.text:
• Pure Functions & Typed Enums: Leverages core language typing and static enumerations for low runtime overhead and strict compiler/linter verification.
  • Alternative - Stateful Domain Entity: Rejected because coupling health calculations to ORM model lifecycles causes concurrency bottlenecks and complex mock setups in testing.
  • Alternative - Externalized Rule Engines (e.g., JSONLogic, Drools): Set aside for foundational domain calculations to prevent configuration drift and preserve compile-time validation, though retained as an optional plug-in for tenant-level override rules.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Batch Snapshot Evaluation: Ingestion pipelines map the pure evaluation function over arrays of partition metrics in worker processes.
  • Threshold Injected Evaluation: Evaluator functions accept an explicit, immutable configuration object specifying threshold boundaries, preserving functional purity while supporting multi-tenant SLA variations.

docs.title: Non-functional characteristics
docs.text:
• Reliability: Eliminates side-effect bugs and race conditions during health aggregation; yields repeatable outputs for any given input.
  • Performance & Latency: Ultra-low evaluation latency (sub-millisecond) bounded strictly by CPU math and string operations without network blocking.
  • Cost & Efficiency: Eliminates redundant I/O round trips during re-scoring; allows evaluations to execute cheaply in-memory across edge or web tiers.
  • Operability: Zero-dependency unit testing simplifies test harness design and regression tracking across environments.

docs.title: Anti-patterns & known pitfalls
docs.text:
• Hidden I/O Leakage: Invoking database queries or logging transports inside calculate_health. Remedy: Maintain an imperative shell, functional core pattern where all I/O completes prior to function invocation.
  • Implicit Threshold Drift: Hardcoding evaluation thresholds in disparate consumer modules. Remedy: Centralize evaluation functions and threshold parameter classes within the shared domain core package.

docs.title: Adoption guidance
docs.text:
1. Extract status evaluation branches from UI components and ORM model hooks into isolated, standalone calculation functions.
  2. Define strict input metric DTOs and return types (HealthStatus and reason collections).
  3. Wire the calling controller or workflow orchestrator to assemble the metrics snapshot and pass it into the pure domain function.
  4. Create standardized test suites verifying corner cases and threshold boundaries without mocking frameworks.

docs.title: Reference Architecture: Registry-Guarded Governance State Machine
Reference Architecture: Registry-Guarded Governance State Machine
Purpose & when to use this
docs.text: The Registry-Guarded Governance State Machine establishes deterministic control boundaries over autonomous agents and programmatic workflows by intercepting all entity lifecycle state transitions and validating them against an explicit transition registry.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• When autonomous agents or LLM-driven workers possess execution authority to modify, promote, or deprecate architectural or business-critical artifacts.
  • When business or governance requirements dictate strict, verifiable lifecycle phases (e.g., candidate -> under_review -> approved -> promoted) that must never be bypassed.
  • When auditability, regulatory compliance, and non-repudiation of entity status changes are mandatory.
  • When automated systems need deterministic guardrails to prevent cascading hallucinations or unauthorized state mutations.

docs.title: When NOT to use this
docs.text:
• When managing transient or stateless workflows where artifacts do not persist across execution boundaries.
  • In early-stage prototyping or unstructured exploratory agent loops where dynamic, ad-hoc state creation is required without fixed governance.
  • For standard CRUD entities where state mutations carry no downstream governance, compliance, or operational risk.

docs.text:

    agent["Autonomous Agent / Worker (Container)"]
    engine["Governance Action Engine (Container)"]
    registry["Transition Registry (Container)"]
    store[("Artifact Store (Data store)")]
    audit["Audit & Observability (External System)"]

    agent -->|1. Propose Transition Action| engine
    engine -->|2. Verify Allowed Transitions| registry
    engine -->|3. Commit Validated Mutation| store
    engine -->|4. Emit State Audit Event| audit

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• GovernanceActionEngine (src/cas_runner/governance/governance_action_engine.py): Mediates mutation requests, validates inputs against the TransitionRegistry, commits state shifts, and blocks unauthorized transitions.
  • TransitionRegistry (src/cas_runner/governance/governance_action_engine.py): Maintains declarative lifecycle state graphs, valid paths, and transition preconditions.
  • Governance Models & Action Descriptors (src/cas_runner/governance/models.py): Defines structured representations of actions (GovernanceAction) and domain-level errors (GovernanceException).
  • Artifact Store: Persists lifecycle states and historical records for architectural entities.

docs.title: Technology choices
docs.text:
• Declarative In-Memory State Registry: Implemented via native language data structures (enums, typed dictionaries) for fast, zero-dependency in-process verification.
  • Strict Typing & Contracts: Pydantic / Python dataclasses enforce contract integrity for incoming actions.
  • Considered and Set Aside: Heavyweight BPMN engines (e.g., Temporal, Camunda) were set aside to eliminate unnecessary network hops and infrastructure overhead for synchronous governance checks.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Strict Synchronous Guard: Rejects invalid transitions immediately with explicit exceptions.
  • Dry-Run Evaluator: Exposes preview capabilities to allow agents to simulate actions without persisting state.
  • Hook-Augmented Enforcer: Triggers policy checks or security scanning webhooks prior to transition commit.

docs.title: Non-functional characteristics
docs.text:
• Reliability: Eliminates invalid states through deterministic boundary checks and transactional commits.
  • Performance & Latency: Sub-millisecond lookup and validation overhead.
  • Cost & Efficiency: Runs embedded in existing application processes without dedicated infrastructure spend.
  • Operability: Emits typed GovernanceException structures and comprehensive audit logs for debugging and tracking.

docs.title: Anti-patterns & known pitfalls
docs.text:
• Direct-Write Bypass: Bypassing the engine to write directly to persistence layers. Remedy: Enforce encapsulation through service boundaries.
  • Wildcard State Transitions: Allowing open-ended * -> * transitions. Remedy: Define explicit source and target state pairs.
  • Deadlock Terminal States: Introducing intermediary states lacking exit transitions. Remedy: Run state graph validation suites to confirm path reachability.

docs.title: Adoption guidance
docs.text:
• Starting Point: Formalize existing artifact states into an enum and configure permissible edges in TransitionRegistry.
  • Migration Path: Deploy engine initially in logging-only mode to capture baseline transition traffic, then enforce strict rejection.
  • Ownership: Enterprise Architecture Governance Team (ideas-to-life-cas).

docs.title: Purpose & when to use this
docs.text: The Rule-Grounded Compliance Evaluation pattern provides automated, deterministic, and machine-readable architectural governance for codebases by verifying pull request deltas against codified rule repositories. Traditional architectural review processes rely heavily on manual human inspection or subjective LLM-as-a-judge evaluations, leading to deployment bottlenecks and inconsistent policy enforcement. This pattern codifies organizational architecture standards and domain boundary rules into machine-enforceable definitions, parsing repository deltas to evaluate violations and yield structured compliance metrics.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• Automated pull request gating: When enforcing domain boundaries, module layering, dependency constraints, or API specifications in continuous integration pipelines.
  • Verifiable audit trails: When enterprise governance mandates reproducible, machine-readable records of compliance posture across release branches.
  • Large-scale monorepos: When cross-team architectural drift occurs frequently due to decoupled development teams modifying shared boundaries.
  • Mitigating subjective LLM drift: When introducing AI-assisted evaluations where model judgments must be strictly anchored to authoritative ground-truth rules rather than generic prompt intuition.

docs.title: When NOT to use this
docs.text:
• Micro-repositories with trivial domain boundaries: Where standard compiler flags or baseline linters (e.g., flake8, eslint) provide exhaustive coverage without custom architectural logic.
  • Dynamic behavioral runtime testing: When verifying system performance, latency, or integration faults under load (utilize integration test suites or synthetic transaction monitors instead).
  • Exploratory prototyping phases: When architecture is intentionally volatile and rapid experimentation precedes the crystallization of domain contracts.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• ComplianceEngine (src/cas_runner/governance/compliance_engine.py): Ingests repository diffs (RawGitDelta), applies matching rules, and coordinates static and semantic analyzers against file changes.
  • Compliance Models (src/cas_runner/governance/models.py): Houses data definitions including ComplianceFinding (capturing violation details, file coordinates, and rule IDs) and ComplianceMetrics (composite score computation).
  • Rule Knowledge Repository (cas-knowledge/rules/): Declarative rule context definitions outlining boundary constraints, forbidden imports, and mandatory architectural patterns.
  • CI Pipeline Runner (.github/workflows/cas-build-validation.yml): Pipeline orchestration layer invoking the evaluation engine on pull request triggers and reporting gate outcomes.

docs.title: Technology choices
docs.text:
• Pydantic v2: Enforces strict typing and serialization for compliance entities and findings.
  • Structured Rule Formats (YAML/JSON): Retains declarative, version-controlled architecture policies. Alternative set aside: Hardcoded code checks, which prevent centralized updates and cross-repository sharing.
  • AST Analysis Engines: Employs structural AST parsing over brittle regex-only scanning.
  • Targeted Model Contexts: Restricts LLM evaluation to localized diff snippets with explicit rule context prompts, setting aside Full-file Prompt LLM Judges to prevent high cost and hallucinations.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Strict Blocking Gate: Fails CI pipelines on any critical violation, preventing merge.
  • Passive Audit & Telemetry: Scans main release branches periodically to track architectural drift trends without interrupting developer workflows.
  • Hybrid Static-Semantic Evaluation: Runs zero-cost AST checks first, deferring only ambiguous semantic cases to model-guided evaluators.

docs.title: Non-functional characteristics
docs.text:
• Reliability: Eliminates subjective review variance by grounding checks in concrete rule sets.
  • Performance & Latency: Optimizes pipeline execution by restricting analysis to git diff hunks (< 5 seconds for standard PRs).
  • Cost & Efficiency: Minimizes token usage by filtering candidates statically before invoking LLMs.
  • Operability: Produces industry-standard SARIF/JSON outputs compatible with common CI/CD dashboard tools.

docs.title: Anti-patterns & known pitfalls
docs.text:
• Unbounded LLM Judge: Relying on generic model prompts without concrete rule references. Remedy: Bind every evaluation to an explicit rule context file.
  • Rule Bloat & Stagnation: Accumulating dead rules that trigger false alarms. Remedy: Enforce rule versioning and deprecation reviews.
  • All-or-Nothing Merge Blocking: Blocking merges on informational style notes. Remedy: Strict tiering between error (blocking) and warning / info (advisory).

docs.title: Adoption guidance
docs.text:
1. Starting Point: Identify 3-5 critical structural boundaries in the system and author them as declarative rules in cas-knowledge.
  2. Migration Path: Deploy in passive reporting mode to measure accuracy and calibrate false-positive rates before turning on blocking gates in CI.

  4. Domain ID: architecture-governance
  5. Initiative ID: automated-ci-guardrails
  6. Owner: Enterprise Architecture & Developer Experience

docs.title: Purpose & when to use this
docs.text: Enforces strict runtime and build-time data validation at all architectural boundaries, preventing non-deterministic, incomplete, or hallucinated payloads from corrupting persistent state.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• Processing outputs from LLM reasoning steps, autonomous agents, or third-party generative models before mutating downstream state.
  • Orchestrating pipelines across distinct execution environments (e.g., CI runners, distributed workers, event buses).
  • Exchanging structured domain payloads across decoupled components where schema drift would cause silent runtime failures.

docs.title: When NOT to use this
docs.text:
• High-frequency internal loops processing raw primitive arrays or unconstrained byte streams where microsecond overhead dominates.
  • Dynamic schema pass-through proxies that intentionally relay arbitrary opaque JSON payloads without inspecting content.
  • Prototyping ephemeral exploratory scripts where domain contracts change continuously within a single monolithic file.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Governance Models & Schema Registry (src/cas_runner/governance/models.py): Defines authoritative, immutable Pydantic V2 domain contracts (GovernanceInventory, ComplianceFinding, GovernanceHealth, GovernanceRisks, GovernanceAction) establishing field types, constraints, and JSON Schema definitions.
  • Steering Models (steering/models.py): Encapsulates task execution manifests, execution boundaries, and prompt-to-model parsing interfaces for autonomous orchestrators.
  • Validation Interceptor / Compliance Engine (src/cas_runner/governance/engine.py): Executes boundary validation against inbound agent and worker payloads, raising deterministic validation errors on schema divergence before storage mutations occur.
  • CI Contract Enforcement Suite (.github/workflows/cas-build-validation.yml): Runs automated pytest suites and schema compatibility assertions on every commit to block backwards-incompatible contract migrations.

docs.title: Technology choices
docs.text:
Selected Pydantic V2 and JSON Schema as primary contract primitives due to compiled Rust-backed validation performance, automatic OpenAPI/JSON schema generation, and native integration with modern Python type checkers.

Alternatives considered and set aside: - Protocol Buffers / gRPC: High compilation overhead and rigid IDL toolchains; unsuitable for direct LLM JSON completion integration. - Marshmallow: Slower serialization and lacks out-of-the-box type annotation alignment with modern Python typing semantics. - Cerberus / Plain Dict Validation: Lacks static typing support, structural validation ergonomics, and automated serialization.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Fail-Fast Strict Validation: The default mode. Rejects non-conformant payloads immediately with validation error telemetry, preventing any side effects.
  • Schema-Guided Re-prompting: Specialized for LLM agents. On contract failure, the Pydantic error details are fed back into the agent context window to re-generate the payload in a bounded retry loop.
  • Schema Migration Tolerant (Lenient Reader): Applied across distributed versions where models configure extra='ignore' or fallback optional fields during deprecation cycles.

docs.title: Non-functional characteristics
docs.text:
• Reliability: Eliminates runtime exceptions caused by KeyError or unexpected NoneType deep inside business logic; ensures atomic boundary rejection.
  • Performance & Latency: Microsecond Pydantic V2 core validation overhead; payload verification consumes <1% of end-to-end agentic or pipeline cycle time.
  • Cost & Efficiency: Prevents downstream processing of malformed data, saving compute, external API quotas, and storage waste.
  • Operability: Structured validation error payloads provide precise field paths, failing values, and expected types, simplifying triage in operational telemetry.

docs.title: Anti-patterns & known pitfalls
docs.text:
• Permissive Dictionary Relaying: Passing unvalidated dict[str, Any] across layer boundaries under the assumption that downstream components will handle missing keys. Remedy: Enforce strict domain models at API entry/exit points.
  • Silent Fallbacks / Masking: Catching schema validation exceptions and defaulting missing fields to empty structures without telemetry, corrupting analytical state. Remedy: Surface structured validation errors and reject invalid payloads explicitly.
  • Dynamic Schemas without Versioning: Changing schema definitions in place without deprecation windows or automated CI migration tests, breaking distributed nodes. Remedy: Use semantic contract versioning and CI integration tests.

docs.title: Adoption guidance
docs.text: Begin adoption at peripheral boundary interfaces (LLM tool response parsers, external HTTP inputs, worker job payloads). Define explicit Pydantic models with strict typing, disallow implicit coercion where precision matters, and wire validation checks directly into CI pipelines via test fixtures. Governance ownership aligns with Core Architecture and Platform Engineering under global initiative scope.

docs.title: Reference Architecture: Sequential Pipeline Flow Runner
Reference Architecture: Sequential Pipeline Flow Runner
Purpose & when to use this
docs.text: The Sequential Pipeline Flow Runner coordinates multi-stage agentic analysis, transformation, and generation tasks using an orchestrated linear runner that passes an explicit, shared execution context between discrete steps. It guarantees deterministic execution order, strict step boundaries, and early short-circuit failure semantics.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• When multi-stage agentic or analysis workflows have strict causal dependencies (e.g., repository diff extraction -> steering projection -> compliance evaluation).
  • When deterministic, auditable execution ordering is mandatory to prevent divergent, looping, or non-terminating autonomous agent behavior.
  • When steps require immutable handoffs via an explicitly validated, shared execution context.
  • When failure in an early stage must reliably short-circuit downstream costly LLM calls or state modifications.

docs.title: When NOT to use this
docs.text:
• When execution stages are embarrassingly parallel, independent evaluations that do not share state or causal dependencies.
  • When dynamic agentic self-reflection or dynamic DAG routing is required where an agent autonomously decides the next step based on runtime tool outputs.
  • When high-frequency, low-latency micro-tasks require sub-millisecond execution without pipeline orchestration overhead.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• FlowRunner (src/cas_runner/runner.py): Orchestrates ordered step invocation, manages lifecycle hooks, enforces short-circuit error handling, and oversees execution context propagation.
  • Step Registry (src/cas_runner/steps/registry.py): Provides catalog lookup and instantiation of typed workflow steps with schema validation for prerequisites and outputs.
  • Shared Flow Context (src/cas_runner/context.py): Encapsulates typed in-memory state, intermediate artifacts, run metadata, and provides immutable or checked mutations between step transitions.
  • Pipeline Steps (src/cas_runner/steps/): Encapsulate individual business or agentic logic (diff extraction, steering projection, governance check) adhering to a uniform step execution protocol.

docs.title: Technology choices
docs.text:
• Runtime Language: Python 3.11+ using explicit typing (typing, dataclasses, and pydantic.BaseModel).
  • Execution Orchestrator: In-process lightweight pipeline controller minimizing runtime dependencies while ensuring determinism in CI/CD environments.
  • State Serialization: JSON-schema backed Pydantic models for predictable context checkpointing and serialization.
  • Alternatives Considered and Set Aside:
  • LangChain / LangGraph: Rejected due to high abstraction churn, heavy dependency footprint, and implicit state mutations.
  • Temporal / Apache Airflow: Set aside for local CI/CD pipelines due to operational infrastructure weight, although recommended for multi-day human-in-the-loop workflows.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Strict Fail-Fast: Execution immediately halts upon any step failure or validation breach. Prevents downstream resource consumption.
  • Compensating Rollback: Executes registered rollback hooks to clean up working directories, ephemeral tokens, or branch state if an intermediate step fails.
  • Speculative Warning: Non-critical observation or linter steps fail soft by logging warnings while allowing the context to advance to subsequent gates.

docs.title: Non-functional characteristics
docs.text:
• Reliability: Eliminates divergent agent loops and non-deterministic state degradation through immutable context boundaries and fail-fast assertions.
  • Performance & Latency: Overhead introduced by the runner is negligible (<5ms per transition). Total latency is bounded by step execution and network IO.
  • Cost & Efficiency: Prevents wasted LLM token spend by short-circuiting prior to expensive model calls when preliminary inputs or checks fail.
  • Operability: Uniform step telemetry provides structured logs, stage durations, and context diffs per stage for clear debugging in CI/CD.

docs.title: Anti-patterns & known pitfalls
docs.text:
• God Context: Dumping unstructured, untyped state into a generic dictionary. Remedy: Enforce Pydantic validation on step boundaries.
  • Side-Channel Mutations: Modifying local filesystem files or global variables without updating the shared context. Remedy: Treat steps as pure functions of context to output.
  • Unbounded Branching: Allowing steps to recursively call other pipelines dynamically. Remedy: Maintain a flat, declarative step configuration.

docs.title: Adoption guidance
docs.text:
• Starting Points: Derive steps from the base step interface, defining input and output schemas. Register steps in src/cas_runner/steps/registry.py.
  • Migration Path: Refactor single-script agent implementations by separating diff ingestion, prompt construction, LLM generation, and evaluation into discrete stages.
  • Ownership: Architecture Domain: Core CAS Runtime; Strategic Initiative: Enterprise Continuous Architecture; Primary Owner: Systems & Architecture Platform Team.

docs.title: Purpose & when to use this
docs.text: Coordinates multi-step agentic and deterministic evaluation tasks through a centralized, linear execution runner with shared context propagation and fail-fast short-circuit semantics.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• Workflow execution requires strict step ordering where downstream phases strictly depend on state, artifacts, or validations from upstream stages.
  • Workflows must enforce deterministic exit conditions, checkpoint validation, and immediate termination upon encountering critical compliance or validation errors.
  • Running in CI/CD automation or CLI runners (e.g., GitHub Actions, local developer terminals) where explicit exit codes, discrete execution stages, and reproducible log traces are required.
  • Governing autonomous or semi-autonomous LLM agent operations that must be constrained within discrete guardrails and explicit operational boundaries.

docs.title: When NOT to use this
docs.text:
• High-throughput streaming or real-time event-driven pipelines requiring microsecond latencies or continuous unbound processing.
  • Highly parallelized map-reduce or fan-out/fan-in workloads where stages have zero data dependencies and sequential scheduling creates unnecessary latency bottlenecks.
  • Dynamic workflow topologies where the next execution stage is dynamically decided via open-ended graph traversal or non-linear state machines.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• FlowRunner Coordinator (src/cas_runner/runner.py): Directs phase progression, evaluates stage exit criteria, enforces timeouts, and manages deterministic fail-fast short circuits across the execution lifecycle.
  • Pipeline Execution Context (src/cas_runner/context.py): Provides an immutable-by-default or controlled mutable state store carrying runtime configuration, accumulated stage outputs, execution metrics, and audit logs.
  • Deterministic Validation Stages (src/cas_runner/stages/validation.py): Executes static checks, schema validation, linting, and policy verification to gate subsequent execution before expensive operations occur.
  • Agentic Execution Stages (src/cas_runner/stages/agentic.py): Interacts with language models and external tool chains within structured input/output bounds to synthesize findings or execute complex reasoning tasks.
  • Artifact Output Store (docs/architecture/): Stores synthesized architectural reports, schema artifacts, execution logs, and serializable run summaries for external consumption.

docs.title: Recommended Choices
docs.text:
• Core Language & Runtime: Python 3.11+ using standard typed dataclasses/Pydantic for context models, ensuring strict runtime schema validation across stages.
  • Orchestration Engine: In-process lightweight sequential runner (FlowRunner) to minimize operational overhead and dependency footprints in headless CI/CD environments.
  • State Management: In-memory context container with JSON/YAML snapshot serialization capability at phase boundaries for checkpointing and replayability.
  • Interface Layer: Click or Typer CLI combined with standard exit codes (0 for success, 1 for validation breach, 2 for unexpected runtime crash) for native CI/CD workflow integration.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered and Set Aside
docs.text:
• Temporal / Prefect / Airflow: Evaluated for enterprise workflow orchestration. Set aside for CAS core execution due to heavyweight infrastructure requirements (workers, databases, web servers) that impede rapid local CLI execution and lightweight GitHub Actions runners.
  • LangChain / LangGraph Agent Loops: Considered for agent orchestration. Set aside as the overarching runner because unconstrained agent loops risk non-deterministic exits, excessive token consumption, and opaque failure modes without strict sequential gating.

docs.title: 1. Strict Stop-on-Failure (Default)
docs.text: Any failure or compliance violation in an upstream stage immediately terminates the pipeline, returning non-zero exit codes and skipping all downstream stages to conserve tokens and provide immediate feedback.

docs.title: 2. Lenient Diagnostic Mode (Collect & Report)
docs.text: Stages continue execution despite non-critical warnings or soft validation failures. The execution context aggregates diagnostic findings across all stages, producing a comprehensive evaluation report at termination.

docs.title: 3. Batched Hybrid Pipeline
docs.text: Independent parallel sub-tasks (e.g., multi-file static analysis or parallel prompt evaluations) are executed concurrently within a discrete sequential stage, synchronizing outputs before proceeding to the next gate.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
• Guarantees idempotent and deterministic stage transitions.
  • Provides checkpointing at discrete stage boundaries, enabling clean post-mortem inspection when failures occur.

docs.title: Performance & Latency
docs.text:
• Minimal orchestration overhead (< 5ms runner overhead per stage transition).
  • Linear time complexity relative to stage count; non-dependent sub-tasks within a stage can leverage async concurrency to avoid sequential blocking.

docs.title: Cost & Efficiency
docs.text:
• Eliminates wasted model API calls and compute expenses by failing fast on deterministic checks before invoking agentic LLM phases.
  • Operates in-memory without persistent backing services or managed orchestration licenses.

docs.title: Operability & Observability
docs.text:
• Structured JSON log emission per stage with monotonic timing metrics, token usage tracking, and explicit exit codes.
  • Self-contained CLI surface allows single-command local reproduction of CI/CD pipeline issues.

docs.title: 1. Context Bloat and Blind Mutation
docs.text:
• Antipattern: Allowing arbitrary stages to indiscriminately mutate or overwrite global state without explicit contracts.
  • Remedy: Use strongly-typed dataclasses where stages receive read-only views of prior outputs and produce dedicated, namespaced stage result objects.

docs.title: 2. Monolithic Stage Execution
docs.text:
• Antipattern: Blurring deterministic validations and stochastic agent prompts into a single massive stage, preventing clean short-circuiting.
  • Remedy: Decompose logic into discrete, single-responsibility phases (e.g., Pre-check -> Generation -> Schema Gating -> Synthesis).

docs.title: 3. Unbounded Sequential Processing
docs.text:
• Antipattern: Executing dozens of completely independent file validations or API calls strictly one after another in sequential mode.
  • Remedy: Employ the Batched Hybrid Pipeline variant to fan out independent checks within a designated stage while preserving sequential phase gating.

docs.title: Migration Path & Starting Points
docs.text:
1. Baseline Implementation: Adopt FlowRunner from src/cas_runner/runner.py as the standard entry point for CLI and automated workflows.
  2. Interface Contract: Implement stages adhering to the standard Stage protocol (execute(context: ExecutionContext) -> StageResult).
  3. Fail-Fast Integration: Place static schema validation and linting at Stage 0 to arrest execution before triggering agentic LLM prompts.

docs.title: Purpose & when to use this
docs.text: Instruments pipeline execution and agent interactions with OpenTelemetry to track latency, token usage, and step errors across complex execution lifecycles.

docs.title: When to use this
docs.text:
• Complex, multi-step LLM and autonomous agent orchestration pipelines where nested tool calls make failure attribution difficult.
  • Environments requiring precise attribution of token consumption, model inference latency, and operational cost across individual agent steps.
  • Distributed agent workflows requiring standardized trace context propagation across heterogeneous services or runtime environments.
  • Regulated or enterprise environments demanding auditable tracking of execution paths and error boundaries.

docs.title: When NOT to use this
docs.text:
• Simple, single-invocation LLM calls or deterministic scripts where standard runtime structured logging provides adequate observability.
  • Extremely low-latency, real-time edge streaming applications where span creation and attribute serialization impose unacceptable execution overhead.
  • Scenarios where complete offline isolation is required and local persistence of trace contexts is unsupported or unnecessary.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Agent Orchestrator (src/cas_runner/orchestrator): Coordinates multi-step agent pipelines, initializes the root trace context, and propagates traceparent metadata across step boundaries.
  • Step Execution Runtime (src/cas_runner/execution): Executes discrete agent steps, wraps tool executions in distinct child spans, and captures prompt tokens, completion tokens, and runtime exceptions.
  • Telemetry & Metric Handler (src/cas_runner/governance/models.py): Encapsulates TraceableMetric contracts, handles sanitization of span attributes, and manages batch exporting to telemetry collectors.
  • Local Telemetry Store (src/cas_runner/knowledge/local_knowledge_provider.py): Provides deterministic local persistence for trace manifests and operational logs for offline evaluation and auditability.
  • OpenTelemetry Collector (external/collector): Ingests OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) traces and metrics, performing enterprise aggregation, routing, and centralized storage integration.

docs.title: Selected Standards & Technologies
docs.text:
• OpenTelemetry API & SDK (opentelemetry-api, opentelemetry-sdk): Standardized, vendor-agnostic specification for distributed traces, metrics, and contextual baggage.
  • OTLP (gRPC / HTTP Protobuf): Industry-standard protocol for pushing instrumentation data to telemetry gateways.
  • Pydantic Data Contracts (TraceableMetric): Guarantees typed enforcement of metric payloads and telemetry schema consistency across agent steps.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered & Set Aside
docs.text:
• Proprietary Vendor Tracing SDKs (e.g., Datadog, New Relic native SDKs): Rejected to prevent vendor lock-in and retain export flexibility across sovereign or hybrid cloud environments.
  • Raw Unstructured Application Logging: Set aside due to high querying overhead, lack of context propagation across asynchronous steps, and inability to build reliable automated latency/cost alerting.
  • Custom In-House Trace Context Headers: Rejected in favor of W3C TraceContext standards natively supported by OpenTelemetry.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Asynchronous Non-Blocking Export (Default): Telemetry spans and metrics are queued in an in-memory batch processor and exported asynchronously to avoid blocking agent inference cycles. Ideal for production execution environments.
  • Synchronous Local File Persistence: Spans and TraceableMetric objects are synchronously flushed to a structured local directory via LocalKnowledgeProvider. Ideal for local evaluation, test suites, and decoupled CI/CD verification where no remote collector is reachable.
  • Redacted Enterprise Mode: Enforces prompt and completion masking prior to span attribute assignment to prevent leakage of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or sensitive proprietary context to monitoring backends.

docs.title: Non-functional characteristics
docs.text:
• Reliability: Failures in tracing or metric export do not interrupt the core agent execution path. Bounded in-memory queues protect process stability under network degradation.
  • Performance & Latency: Overhead is restricted to < 2ms per step. Batch span processors flush asynchronously to prevent tail latency degradation.
  • Cost & Efficiency: Standardized token recording enables instant query visibility into cost drivers per tenant, prompt revision, and tool call.
  • Operability: Adheres to W3C distributed tracing standards, ensuring compatibility across enterprise observability suites (Jaeger, Prometheus, Grafana Tempo, Datadog).

docs.title: Anti-patterns & known pitfalls
docs.text:
• Unsanitized Payload Injection in Span Attributes: Do not write raw user prompts, PII, or full responses directly into attributes. Use redaction utilities and store structured metadata instead.
  • Synchronous Export in Hot Inference Paths: Avoid SimpleSpanProcessor in production workloads to prevent network latency from inflating agent execution durations.
  • Context Severing in Asynchronous Sub-Tasks: Always propagate context explicitly into spawned concurrent tasks or worker processes using context.attach().

docs.title: Adoption guidance
docs.text:
1. SDK Baseline: Add opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk to runtime dependencies.
  2. Metric Definition: Adopt TraceableMetric models for standardizing step-level execution metrics.
  3. Context Instrumentation: Ensure agent execution handlers initialize traces and properly nest sub-steps.
  4. Export Configuration: Direct OTLP exporter to local collectors or enterprise observability backends.

docs.title: Governance State
docs.text:
CAS governance is in transition from a template-ready, manually-triggered model to an operationally governed, rules-driven model.

  • Authoritative artifacts: ADRs (11), Architecture Work (41 instances in work/, of which 30 are proposed), AEM (6 daily versions), AID (5 versions), Alignment Reports (5 versions).
  • Rule set: 19 global rules active in the alignment engine; rule conflicts and prompt-rule audit reports produced (5 conflict reports, 4 prompt audits).
  • Lifecycle coverage: All governance artifacts carry schema-validated frontmatter; rule precedence hierarchy enforced (rule-precedence-hierarchy); no project-scoped rules exist.
  • Provenance: Architecture Work is now the planning source of truth; AEM and AID are derived.
  • Human-in-the-loop: Enforced by rule-system-proposes-architect-decides and rule-decision-status-drives-stage.

Governance maturity: Emerging → Active. Structure is in place; velocity is constrained by the proposal backlog and a schema-compliance gap.

docs.title: Architecture State
docs.text:
Major architectural structures, models, and patterns currently in operation:

  • Workflow Execution Model — Runner / Workflow / Knowledge Provider separation, with ReasoningExecutionContract mediating prompt-to-LLM interaction.
  • Architecture Knowledge Layer — knowledge/global/ and knowledge/projects/<project>/ partitioning, with templates, rules, patterns, decisions, maps, intent, alignment, and ingestion directories.
  • Architecture Work Registry — Persistent, schema-validated planning layer.
  • AEM / AID / Alignment chain — Generated governance dashboard artifacts.
  • Rules Context Loader — Loads global and project rules into the reasoning context at execution time.
  • Steering Projection — Git delta → knowledge artifact pipeline (steering-projection-flow).
  • LLM Provider Abstraction — Provider-agnostic LLM boundary with structured output.
  • Pattern Catalogue — 17 patterns persisted as global architecture knowledge.
  • Architecture Lineage — Module-level capability tracking via capabilities/lineage.yaml.

Established patterns (representative): architecture-workflow-loop, build-time-governance, contract-first-architecture, deterministic-core-selective-augmentation, heuristic-driven-arbitration, llm-provider-abstraction-boundary, orchestrator-managed-pipeline, prompt-as-code-separation, prompt-schema-contracts-as-architecture, structured-output-via-schema, typed-execution-context.

  • Automation capabilities: Runtime-native Architecture Work generation (operational), CI workflows cas-managed-steering-sync.yml and cas-portal-publish.yml (active), cas run <flow> orchestration CLI (active), lineage tracking (automatic).
  • Operational governance maturity: Emerging. Automation exists for the core loop (Runner + AEM + AID + Alignment + AW); enforcement automation (CI validation enforcing CAS skill compliance) is proposed but not yet implemented.
  • Trust calibration: Heuristic governance health model is the approved Phase 1 mechanism (ADR-030), and the dashboard is read-only intelligence.

docs.title: Strategic Gaps
docs.text:
Evidence-backed gaps between current and intended architecture:

  1. YAML ADR migration is incomplete. rule-decision-schema-must-be-structured is active; 11 ADRs persist as narrative Markdown. (Alignment HIGH; aw-2026-06-06-01 proposed; AEM READY.)
  2. Core Orchestration Pipeline ADR is missing. Foundational decision provenance for the orchestration pipeline is absent. (Alignment HIGH; aw-2026-06-06-02 proposed; AEM READY.)
  3. Governance velocity bottleneck. 30 Architecture Work proposals vs 2 accepted in the current AEM (proposed:accepted ratio of 15:1, exceeding the 5:1 heuristic threshold from the AID). (Alignment HIGH; AID risk.)
  4. Automated CI validation for CAS skills is absent. No enforced guardrail at PR time. (Alignment MEDIUM; AID risk.)
  5. Business Intent knowledge model is absent. Traceability from business requirement → ADR → pattern → code is not yet possible. (Alignment MEDIUM; aw-2026-05-31-006 proposed.)
  6. Code Intelligence is absent. No structural code analysis, no automated drift detection. (AID long-term roadmap; aw-2026-05-31-007 proposed.)
  7. AID/AEM business_traceability coverage is low. (AID coverage field.)
  8. Project-scoped rules layer is empty. All rules are global; knowledge/projects/*/rules/ is unused. (Rule conflict report note.)

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: The ideas-to-life-cas project is transitioning from a template-ready documentation model to an operational Architecture Intelligence Platform. While foundational structures (CAS Runner, Knowledge Provider, and Governance Portal) are operational, the system is currently 'partially aligned' due to significant backlog pressure (22 unprogressed proposals) and a persistence lag where implementation progress has outpaced formal decision recording (ADRs).

docs.title: Architecture Evolution Summary
docs.text: Observable evolution includes the institutionalization of the Architecture Work Registry as the authoritative backlog, the implementation of a published Governance Portal (MkDocs/GitHub Pages), and the abstraction of the Knowledge Provider to decouple workflows from storage. The system has moved from manual execution to semi-automated orchestration via the CAS Runner.

docs.title: Architecture Evolution
docs.text: The project is on a trajectory toward 'Continuous Architecture Governance'. Maturity in structural contracts and operational guidance is high, but governance execution maturity is currently bottlenecked by a 15:1 governance velocity ratio, necessitating a shift toward automated Detect-Analyse-Execute loops.

docs.title: Capability Landscape
docs.text: Operational capabilities include the CAS Runner, Knowledge Provider Abstraction, and Governance Portal. Active capabilities include the Architecture Work Registry and Alignment Engine. Emerging capabilities include Business Intent Integration, Code Intelligence, and the Architecture Knowledge Graph.

docs.title: Capability Dependencies
docs.text: The Architecture Work Registry serves as the source for AEM and AID generation. The Knowledge Provider Abstraction is a prerequisite for the Architecture Knowledge Graph. The Alignment Engine depends on the Rule Context and the Workflow Execution Model.

docs.title: Initiative Landscape
docs.text: Governance Foundation is active and stabilizing. Architecture Work Registry is active with its authoritative status accepted. Operational Intelligence and ReasoningOps are in the proposed/planning phase, focusing on cross-project lineage and continuous evaluation loops.

docs.title: Governance State
docs.text: Governance is currently 'partially aligned'. The primary gap is 'Backlog Pressure' (22 proposals vs 6 completed items). A 'Persistence Lag' exists where core components like the Workflow Execution Model are implemented but lack formal ADR acceptance. Governance is shifting from periodic review to a participation model embedded in delivery.

docs.title: Architecture State
docs.text: The architecture is defined by a standardized Workflow Execution Model (Runner/Workflow/KnowledgeProvider). The system has adopted a 'Rules as Authority' model over separate policies. The Architecture Work Registry is now the single source of truth for architectural change, resolving previous issues with planning state loss during regeneration.

docs.title: Intelligence State
docs.text: Intelligence is currently focused on drift detection via the Alignment Engine. Future state plans include an Architecture Intelligence Layer for signal detection, pattern discovery, and a Knowledge Graph for multi-hop lineage analysis across the portfolio.

docs.title: Operational State
docs.text: Operational maturity is supported by a live MkDocs portal and a standardized runner. Automated CI validation for CAS skill enforcement is proposed to prevent architectural drift. The current operating model relies on 'Prevent-Detect-Feedback' loops.

docs.title: Architecture State Metrics
docs.text: Total Architecture Work items: 30. Status distribution: 22 Proposed, 6 Done, 1 Accepted, 1 Dummy. Alignment findings: 3 High, 3 Medium. Governance velocity ratio: 15:1.

docs.title: Strategic Gaps
docs.text: 1. Persistence Lag: Implementation (DONE) outpaces formal ADRs. 2. Intent Definition Gap: Lack of formal Business Intent schema prevents full traceability. 3. Backlog Pressure: System generates proposals faster than human validation capacity. 4. Derivation Mismatch: AEM stages are implementation-driven rather than decision-driven.

docs.title: Observed State
docs.text: The system exhibits a robust structural foundation with active alignment reporting and a published governance surface, but implementation reality is frequently ahead of governed decision records.

docs.title: Interpreted State
docs.text: The project has successfully established 'Governance Foundation v1' but is struggling with the transition to 'Continuous Governance' due to the manual overhead of processing high-volume architectural signals.

docs.title: Hypothesised State
docs.text: Implementing a 'Governance Action Framework' and automated remediation signals within the Alignment Engine will be required to reduce the 15:1 velocity bottleneck and clear the proposal backlog.

docs.title: Confidence Assessment
docs.text: High confidence in the structural and foundational state based on comprehensive baseline and AEM data. Medium confidence in implementation alignment due to the identified persistence lag and unpopulated project-specific patterns.

docs.title: Vision & Strategy
docs.text:
Latest State

Showing latest version: cas-future-vision (N/A)

docs.title: 1. Framing
docs.text:
CAS has reached a stable baseline as a decision-driven architecture system:

Code / Conversations → Architecture Work (Aw) → Patterns → Decisions (ADR) → AEM → AID

The next evolution is to transform CAS into an Architecture Intelligence Platform that connects:

Business Intent ↔ Architecture ↔ Code ↔ Decisions

docs.title: Current Scope (Solved)
docs.text:
• Extract patterns from code and learnings
  • Govern architecture via ADRs
  • Maintain consistent architecture state (AEM)
  • Generate architectural intent (AID)

docs.title: Target Scope (Next)
docs.text:
CAS should answer:

- How to connect business intent to architecture and implementation?
- How to stop bad structure from being created in the first place, and catch what still slips through?
- How to continuously align target architecture (AID) with actual implementation (Code) and system state (AEM)?
- Why was this system built this way?
- Does the implementation match the intended architecture?
- How does business intent map to architecture decisions?
- What is the impact of a change across the system and portfolio?

docs.title: 3.1 Business Layer Integration
docs.text: Goal: Connect business artefacts to architecture and implementation.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Business Requirements Documents (BRD)
  • Business Cases
  • Portfolio / initiative definitions
  • Strategic objectives

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Extract intent signals from business artefacts
  • Link business intent → patterns → decisions
  • Trace:
Business Requirement → ADR → Pattern → Code

docs.title: Example Use Case
docs.text: • "Which architectural decisions support this business capability?"

docs.title: 3.2 Code Intelligence Layer
docs.text: Goal: Move from pattern extraction to full code understanding.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Structural analysis of codebases
  • Identify architectural boundaries, modules, and dependencies
  • Map code → patterns → architecture
  • Detect deviations from intended architecture (AID)
  • Prevent (stop) bad structure from being created in the first place, and catch (detect & correct) what still slips through

docs.title: Example Use Cases
docs.text:
• "Explain how this system is structured"
  • "Where does the implementation violate the architecture?"
  • "Implmenent a new feature or refactor with confidence by understanding the architectural context"

docs.title: 3.3 Architecture Alignment
docs.text: Goal: Continuously align intent vs reality.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Compare:
AID (intent) vs Code (implementation)
AID vs Solution Architecture Documents
AID vs AEM (state)
  • Detect gaps:
  • Missing components
  • Incorrect boundaries
  • Drift over time

docs.title: Example Use Case
docs.text: • "Show the gap between target architecture and current implementation"

docs.title: 3.4 ReasoningOps & GovernanceOps
docs.text: Goal: Transform architecture governance from periodic review activities into continuously participating operational capabilities.

docs.title: ReasoningOps
docs.text: ReasoningOps enables architecture intelligence generation through structured operational reasoning loops.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Convert conversations, implementation activity, architecture work, and operational signals into architectural intelligence
  • Continuously evaluate alignment between intent, implementation, patterns, decisions, and system state
  • Generate architecture evolution recommendations
  • Surface governance drift, capability evolution, and emerging patterns
  • Support architecture participation throughout delivery rather than only during review events

docs.title: Example Use Cases
docs.text:
• "What architectural tensions are emerging across recent implementation activity?"
  • "Which governance signals require architectural attention?"
  • "What architecture work should be prioritised next?"

docs.title: GovernanceOps
docs.text: GovernanceOps operationalises governance as a lightweight, continuously active participation model embedded within delivery workflows.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Governance-aware workflow participation
  • Continuous validation and trust calibration
  • Governance signal lifecycle management
  • Pattern evolution and governance refinement
  • Operational intelligence integration into architectural decision-making
  • Execution-driven governance evolution

docs.title: Example Use Cases
docs.text:
• "How is governance evolving based on operational execution?"
  • "Which validated implementation patterns should become governed architectural patterns?"
  • "Where is governance drift emerging across workflows?"

docs.title: Operational Model

docs.title: 1. Framing
docs.text:
CAS has reached a stable baseline as a decision-driven architecture system:

Code / Conversations → Architecture Work (Aw) → Patterns → Decisions (ADR) → AEM → AID

The next evolution is to transform CAS into an Architecture Intelligence Platform that connects:

Business Intent ↔ Architecture ↔ Code ↔ Decisions

docs.title: Current Scope (Solved)
docs.text:
• Extract patterns from code and learnings
  • Govern architecture via ADRs
  • Maintain consistent architecture state (AEM)
  • Generate architectural intent (AID)

docs.title: Target Scope (Next)
docs.text:
CAS should answer:

- How to connect business intent to architecture and implementation?
- How to stop bad structure from being created in the first place, and catch what still slips through?
- How to continuously align target architecture (AID) with actual implementation (Code) and system state (AEM)?
- Why was this system built this way?
- Does the implementation match the intended architecture?
- How does business intent map to architecture decisions?
- What is the impact of a change across the system and portfolio?

  • Support architecture participation throughout delivery rather than only during review events

docs.title: Example Use Cases

  • "Which governance signals require architectural attention?"
  • "What architecture work should be prioritised next?"

  • Operational intelligence integration into architectural decision-making
  • Execution-driven governance evolution

  • "Which validated implementation patterns should become governed architectural patterns?"
  • "Where is governance drift emerging across workflows?"
